title: Maintain fallback model-variant compatibility matrix for tokenizer/context/tooling parity
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Background:
Redwood's smart routing subsystem needs to safely and deterministically select fallback model variants when a primary model is unavailable due to capacity, region, or tier constraints. In practice, a fallback candidate must match on several compatibility dimensions: tokenizer/tokenizer_id (byte vs. unicode handling and token IDs), max context window, function/tooling support (function calling, streaming, structured outputs), embedding dimensionality (for embedding fallbacks), and any special runtime flags (KV-layout or quantization idiosyncrasies).

Problem statement:
We currently have ad-hoc checks in routing logic that compare only model family and approximate tokenization behavior. This has caused routing incidents where fallback to a quantized variant or a trimmed-context variant produced misaligned token IDs or dropped tool calls, causing downstream hallucinations or tooling failures. We need a canonical compatibility matrix and automation to keep it accurate as new model variants are onboarded.

Goal / Acceptance criteria:
- A single source-of-truth compatibility matrix (CSV/JSON) in the model-catalog repo describing, per model-variant: tokenizer_id, tokenizer_version, max_context_tokens, tool_calling: yes/no, streaming_support: yes/no, embedding_dims (if applicable), canonical_token_mapping_note, known_incompatibilities.
- Routing logic (smart-router) consults the matrix and rejects fallbacks that fail critical parity checks (tokenizer ID mismatch OR missing tool_calling when request includes tool calls). Non-critical mismatches (e.g., smaller context window) trigger automatic prefix-truncation hint or explicit fallback with warning depending on policy.
- CI check (GitHub Action) that validates any model-catalog change against unit tests and a compatibility-linter; PRs that add variants must populate all matrix fields.
- Backfill current deployed catalog for the top 25 models + variants with verified fields.
- Dashboard in Console showing fallback compatibility coverage and metrics on fallback occurrences and rejects.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Define schema and storage: create model_compatibility.csv and model_compatibility.json schema in the model-catalog repo (serving-team/model-catalog). Fields: model_key, variant_key, tokenizer_id, tokenizer_version, max_context, supports_function_calling, supports_streaming, embedding_dim, kv_cache_layout, quantization_profile, notes, last_verified.
2) Update onboarding checklist and PR templates: require compatibility fields for new model variants and a verification step.
3) Build a compatibility-linter GitHub Action (model-compat-checker) that rejects incomplete entries and runs a small tokenization parity unit test (tokenize sample prompts using the variant and a canonical tokenizer service).
4) Incorporate into smart-router: new compatibility gate that is consulted during routing decisions. Add opt-in config flags to allow tolerant policies for older customers.
5) Backfill: run a one-off verification job that tokenizes a small canonical prompt set across variants to detect tokenizer_id mismatches. Flag ambiguous cases for manual review.
6) Console: add a per-model compatibility view and an SLO for fallback rejects and mismatches.

Engineering tasks (expected scope):
- Draft schema + unit tests (Daniel)
- Implement model-compat-checker Action (Daniel, +2)
- Integrate compatibility gate in smart-router + fallthrough policies (runtime team)
- Backfill verification job and results dashboard (data infra + console)
- Update onboarding docs and PR templates (docs + onboarding)

Trade-offs and decisions to make:
- Strict vs tolerant routing: Strict parity reduces incidents but reduces availability. We should default to STRICT for tool-calling requests and TOLERANT for simple text generation (configurable per customer/tier).
- Tokenizer vs byte-compatibility: Some older quantized variants use a byte-level tokenizer; mapping may be lossy. For such variants we will mark tokenizer_id as incompatible and avoid routing for tool-calling or structured-output requests.
- Automation vs manual verification: Tokenization parity tests will catch most cases but not all (edge-case token splitting). Manual review will be required for flagged ambiguous variants.

Risks:
- False positives from the parity linter could block legitimate variants if tokenizer services are out-of-sync. Mitigation: fall back to a permissive override and add alerts for linter failures.
- Performance: extra checks in the hot path could add latency. Mitigation: cache matrix lookups and evaluate only once per routing decision; warm caches in routing pools.

Test plan / QA:
- Unit tests for compatibility-linter (mock tokenizers)
- Integration tests: simulate routing with primary unavailable and assert that fallbacks chosen conform to expected behavior for cases: (A) tokenizer mismatch; (B) smaller context window; (C) missing tool_calling; (D) embedding dimensionality mismatch.
- Canary rollout to dedicated region with telemetry for fallback rejects and user-facing error rates.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): Create schema, linter, and backfill top 10 models. Non-blocking rollout: routing will log compatibility decisions but not enforce.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): Enforce parity for tool-calling and structured outputs only. Enable CI checks for new model variant PRs.
- Phase 3 (1 week): Full enforcement by default for hosted API; allow per-customer toggles for legacy behavior; add Console visibility and alerting.

Open questions / Action items:
- Do we treat tokenizer_version as authoritative or derive from tokenizer artifact hash? (ACTION: decide with model-team)
- What is the authoritative list of sample prompts for tokenization parity tests? (ACTION: QA + research create canon_prompts.md)
- How granular should quantization_profile be (e.g., quant8q, int4, custom kernel flags)?
